claim: In the 21-day habit challenge, the habit was cut the day before to 250 burpees from the target of 500, without feeling bad
As came up in conversation, being okay with scaling back habits takes a mental and emotional adjustment
You can scale habits back, even a lot, and still get a lot of the benefit, because you keep wiring them as the pattern: maybe you normally meditate for 20 minutes and cut it to three

Growing up a big Michael Jordan fan, grateful to have watched "an incredible competitor, certainly an imperfect human as we all are". He had plenty of games that were not noteworthy, like 16 points and five rebounds. Does anybody remember them? No. Did they stop him from becoming who he was meant to be? No. He showed up and, even when his output wasn't the same as the night before, kept demonstrating a pattern of showing up and giving what he had that day
Like Michael Jordan's games that were not noteworthy, scaling back your habits won't stop your journey or your growth
Scaling back your habits is okay; it keeps you marching forward
Show up and give what you have: if it's 500 burpees and you've got a hundred today, do a hundred, "Infinitely better than doing zero"

Day 5 of the 21-day habit challenge, among lots of other self-care habits tracked: 500 burpees done, with burpee strength coming back (their own animal, a cardio-strength combination), meditation, and some amazing human connection
name: Habits and tracking

claim: There's zero need to feel bad about scaling back a habit; recognize it as the win it is, doing something instead of notching a zero
If you have to scale a habit back over and over again, something needs to change: maybe when you do it, where it fits in your day, what the habit is, or the time in your life
On occasional days of scaling a habit back, don't sweat it or beat yourself up
